Shielding and enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications such as web servers, databases and the Agent.

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. The shield protects resources (for example, files, registry keys, processes) that are part of the protected application. A shielding event indicates that a process or user not related to the protected application is attempting to access one of its resources.

Enveloping an application protects resources not belonging to an application from being accessed by that application. The envelope contains all resources the application requires (for example, files, registry keys, processes). McAfee HIP allows the application to access the resources inside the envelope. Any attempt to access resources outside the envelope can signify malicious behavior and is blocked. Therefore, an envelope event indicates that a process or user related to the enveloped application is attempting to access a resource that is not inside the application's envelope.

Setting.value: MSSQL Aux. Shielding - Service Modification

Setting.name: SignatureNotes
Setting.value:
(Refer to KB article 51504 for details about supported platforms.) This event indicates that an attempt to stop or change the settings of an auxiliary MSSQL service was detected. See Advanced Details to see the service involved.
The services covered by MSSQL Auxiliary Shielding are MSDTC, MSSEARCH, MSSQLOLAPService, and MSSQLServerADHelper.
Shielding and Enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications (such as Web Servers, databases and the Agent).

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. The shield protects resources (files, registry keys, user accounts, processes, etc.) that are part of the protected application. A Shielding event indicates that a process or user not related to the protected application is attempting to access one of the resources of the protected application.

Enveloping an application protects resources not belonging to an application from being accessed by that application. The envelope contains all resources the application requires (files, registry keys, user accounts, processes, etc.). McAfee HIP allows the application to access the resources inside the envelope. Any attempt to access resources outside the envelope can signify malicious behavior and is blocked. Setting.name: SignatureName
Setting.value: Windows Agent Shielding - Service Access

Setting.name: SignatureNotes
Setting.value:
(Refer to KB article 51504 for details about supported platforms.) This signature is one of the self-protection features of the Agent. Agent resources - which include files, registry keys, and services - are protected so that an attacker cannot disable the Agent so that it no longer offers protection. Only the Agent process is authorized to manipulate resources associated with itself. An attempt to modify any resources may indicate an intrusion event.
Shielding and enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications such as web servers, databases and the Agent.

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. The shield protects resources (for example, files, registry keys, processes) that are part of the protected application. A shielding event indicates that a process or user not related to the protected application is attempting to access one of its resources.

Enveloping an application protects resources not belonging to an application from being accessed by that application. The envelope contains all resources the application requires (for example, files, registry keys, processes). McAfee HIP allows the application to access the resources inside the envelope. Any attempt to access resources outside the envelope can signify malicious behavior and is blocked. Therefore, an envelope event indicates that a process or user related to the enveloped application is attempting to access a resource that is not inside the application's envelope.

(Refer to KB article 51504 for details about supported platforms.) This event indicates an attempt to start, stop or change the settings of a service by one of the Microsoft IIS processes.
Shielding and enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications such as web servers, databases and the Agent.

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. The shield protects resources (for example, files, registry keys, processes) that are part of the protected application. A shielding event indicates that a process or user not related to the protected application is attempting to access one of its resources.

Enveloping an application protects resources not belonging to an application from being accessed by that application. The envelope contains all resources the application requires (for example, files, registry keys, processes). McAfee HIP allows the application to access the resources inside the envelope. Any attempt to access resources outside the envelope can signify malicious behavior and is blocked. Therefore, an envelope event indicates that a process or user related to the enveloped application is attempting to access a resource that is not inside the application's envelope.

Shielding and enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications such as web servers, databases and the Agent.

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. The shield protects resources (for example, files, registry keys, processes) that are part of the protected application. A shielding event indicates that a process or user not related to the protected application is attempting to access one of its resources.

Enveloping an application protects resources not belonging to an application from being accessed by that application. The envelope contains all resources the application requires (for example, files, registry keys, processes). McAfee HIP allows the application to access the resources inside the envelope. Any attempt to access resources outside the envelope can signify malicious behavior and is blocked. Therefore, an envelope event indicates that a process or user related to the enveloped application is attempting to access a resource that is not inside the application's envelope.

Shielding and enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications from abnormal activities.

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. (Refer to KB article 51504 for details about supported platforms.) This event indicates an attempt for an unauthorized process to stop or change the settings of one of the VMWare Server services. This signature does not protect against a user manually modifying or disabling the services.

Shielding and enveloping are the framework used by McAfee HIP to protect applications from abnormal activities.

Shielding an application provides protection of the application against external access. The shield protects resources (for example, files, registry keys, processes) that are part of the protected application. A shielding event indicates that a process or user not related to the protected application is attempting to access one of its resources.

Enveloping an application protects resources not belonging to an application from being accessed by that application. The envelope contains all resources the application requires (for example, files, registry keys, processes). McAfee HIP allows the application to access the resources inside the envelope. Any attempt to access resources outside the envelope can signify malicious behavior and is blocked. Therefore, an envelope event indicates that a process or user related to the enveloped application is attempting to access a resource that is not inside the application's envelope.
